accepted.s:
Which one of the following pairs is correctly matched?

Mission — Agency/Country
accepted.x: Europa Clipper is a NASA mission aimed at studying Jupiter’s moon Europa. ExoMars is associated with ESA and Roscosmos, Psyche with NASA, and Nuri with South Korea.
accepted.tq: Start from the sure agency–mission pair and eliminate swapped agencies.
accepted.sec: Foreign missions and vehicles → agency + target  [APPSC]

accepted.s: ExoMars is primarily associated with the search for signs of life on which celestial body?
accepted.x: ExoMars is an ESA mission undertaken with Roscosmos involvement to search for signs of life on Mars.
accepted.tq: Directly identify the target body of a named mission.
accepted.sec: Foreign missions and vehicles → agency + target  [APPSC]

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements:
1. Chang’e-3 achieved the first soft landing on the Moon since 1976.
2. Chang’e-4 achieved the first soft landing on the far side of the Moon.
3. Yutu-2 is associated with Chang’e-4.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: All three statements are correct. Chang’e-3 landed softly in 2013, Chang’e-4 made the first far-side soft landing in 2019, and its rover was Yutu-2.
accepted.tq: Check each statement against the mission’s date, achievement and rover association.
accepted.sec: Foreign missions and vehicles → agency + target  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Chang’e-6, launched by China, is particularly associated with which achievement?
o: Testing the first crewed flight around the Moon
Returning samples from the far side of the Moon
accepted.x: Chang’e-6 conducted a far-side lunar sample-return mission in 2024.
accepted.tq: Distinguish closely related missions of the same lunar programme by their specific achievement.
accepted.sec: Foreign missions and vehicles → agency + target  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which of the following statements regarding the Artemis programme is correct?
o: It is an ESA programme for studying Europa.
It is a Japanese programme for landing on Mars.
It is a Chinese programme for commercial Earth observation.
It is a NASA programme intended to return humans to the Moon.
accepted.x: Artemis is NASA’s programme for returning humans to the Moon. India signed the Artemis Accords in 2023 and was invited to NASA’s Moon Base programme.
accepted.tq: Use the programme’s stated objective to separate it from other space missions.
accepted.sec: Foreign missions and vehicles → agency + target  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which one of the following statements about the Artemis missions is correct?
o: Artemis I was an uncrewed SLS-Orion test in 2022.
Artemis II was the first Artemis landing on the Moon.
Artemis III was the first uncrewed SLS-Orion test.
Artemis IV was completed as the first crewed lunar landing in 2024.
accepted.x: Artemis I was an uncrewed SLS-Orion test conducted in 2022. The stated programme plan places the Artemis III crewed Earth-orbit test in 2027 and the first Artemis landing attempt under Artemis IV in 2028.
accepted.tq: Trap the interchange of mission numbers and their assigned phases.
accepted.sec: Foreign missions and vehicles → agency + target  [APPSC]

accepted.s:
Match List-I with List-II:

List-I (Mission/vehicle)
a. Europa Clipper
b. Psyche
c. SuperView
 d. Nuri

List-II (Target or purpose)
i. Commercial high-resolution Earth observation
 ii. Jupiter’s moon Europa
 iii. Metal-rich asteroid 16 Psyche
 iv. South Korea’s indigenous launch vehicle

Select the correct answer using the code given below:
accepted.x: Europa Clipper targets Europa, Psyche targets asteroid 16 Psyche, SuperView provides commercial high-resolution Earth observation, and Nuri is South Korea’s indigenous launch vehicle.
accepted.tq: Begin with the distinctive target 16 Psyche and then complete the remaining pairs.
accepted.sec: Foreign missions and vehicles → agency + target  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which one of the following is correctly matched?
o: Moon Impact Probe — NASA’s 2009 polar-crater impactor
SLIM — Japan’s fifth-nation soft landing on the Moon
Luna-25 — Successful first Russian soft landing on the Moon in 2023
LCROSS — First spacecraft to hit the Moon in 1959
accepted.x: Japan’s SLIM achieved the country’s soft landing on the Moon and was described as the ‘Moon sniper’. Luna-25 crashed before landing, Luna 2 was the first lunar impactor in 1959, and India’s MIP was the 2008 impact probe.
accepted.tq: Find the correctly matched mission and reject swapped dates, agencies and achievements.
accepted.sec: Foreign missions and vehicles → agency + target  [APPSC]

accepted.s:
Arrange the following space-shuttle events in chronological order:
A. First flight of Columbia
B. Repair of the Solar Maximum Mission satellite
C. Loss of Challenger
D. Loss of Columbia during re-entry
accepted.x: The sequence is Columbia’s first flight in 1981, Solar Maximum Mission repair in 1984, Challenger’s loss in 1986, and Columbia’s loss during re-entry in 2003.
accepted.tq: Fix the earliest and latest events first, then arrange the middle events by year.
accepted.sec: Space history - FIRST satellite repaired in orbit, space shuttle missions  [APPSC]

accepted.s: The first satellite repaired in orbit was which of the following?
accepted.x: NASA’s Solar Maximum Mission satellite was repaired by the crew of Space Shuttle Challenger in April 1984 during mission STS-41C.
accepted.tq: Directly identify the unique satellite associated with the first in-orbit repair.
accepted.sec: Space history - FIRST satellite repaired in orbit, space shuttle missions  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which one of the following statements is correct regarding India’s early space milestones?
o: SLV-3 was first used for Aryabhata in 1975.
Aryabhata was launched in 1975 using a Soviet rocket.
Aryabhata made India the sixth nation to launch a satellite indigenously.
Rohini was launched in 1975 using a Soviet rocket.
accepted.x: Aryabhata, India’s first satellite, was launched in 1975 on a Soviet rocket. In 1980, SLV-3 launched Rohini, making India the sixth nation to launch a satellite indigenously.
accepted.tq: Separate the satellite, launch vehicle and year in two closely related milestones.
accepted.sec: Space history - FIRST satellite repaired in orbit, space shuttle missions  [APPSC]

accepted.s: India’s first interplanetary mission, launched on PSLV-C25, was designated as which of the following?
accepted.x: Mangalyaan was India’s first interplanetary mission and was also known as the Mars Orbiter Mission. It was launched on PSLV-C25.
accepted.tq: Identify the alternate official name of the mission from its launch vehicle association.
accepted.sec: Mangalyaan - FIRST-attempt record, rank, orbit, payloads  [other exams]

accepted.s: Which one of the following achievements is associated with Mangalyaan?
o: India became the first country to return samples from Mars.
India became the first country to soft-land on the Moon.
India became the first country to land a rover on the far side of the Moon.
India became the first country to reach Mars orbit on its maiden attempt.
accepted.x: India reached Mars orbit on its maiden attempt through Mangalyaan. It also made India the first Asian nation to orbit Mars.
accepted.tq: Distinguish an orbital achievement from landing and sample-return achievements.
accepted.sec: Mangalyaan - FIRST-attempt record, rank, orbit, payloads  [other exams]

accepted.s: ISRO became the fourth space agency to place a spacecraft in Mars orbit after which sequence of agencies?
accepted.x: ISRO was the fourth space agency to orbit Mars, after NASA, Roscosmos and ESA.
accepted.tq: Use the stated rank and identify the three agencies preceding it.
accepted.sec: Mangalyaan - FIRST-attempt record, rank, orbit, payloads  [other exams]

accepted.s: Which one of the following is NOT a payload carried by Mangalyaan?
accepted.x: Mangalyaan carried the Methane Sensor for Mars, Mars Colour Camera, MENCA, Lyman Alpha Photometer and Thermal Infrared Imaging Spectrometer. Moon Mineralogy Mapper was a Chandrayaan-1 payload.
accepted.tq: Find the instrument belonging to a different mission rather than the named mission.
accepted.sec: Mangalyaan - FIRST-attempt record, rank, orbit, payloads  [other exams]

accepted.s: The orbit of Mangalyaan around Mars was described as:
accepted.x: Mangalyaan was placed in a highly elliptical orbit around Mars.
accepted.tq: Discriminate the mission’s actual orbit from familiar Earth-orbit terms.
accepted.sec: Mangalyaan - FIRST-attempt record, rank, orbit, payloads  [other exams]

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements about Mangalyaan:
1. It was designed for a six-month mission.
2. It functioned for approximately eight years.
3. Contact with it was lost in 2022.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: Mangalyaan was designed for six months but operated for about eight years, and contact was lost in 2022. Therefore, all three statements are correct.
accepted.tq: Check the planned duration, actual performance and termination fact separately.
accepted.sec: Mangalyaan - FIRST-attempt record, rank, orbit, payloads  [other exams]

accepted.s: In a two-body system, the points at which a small object can remain in balance are known as:
accepted.x: Lagrange points are five points, L1 to L5, in a two-body system where a small object can remain in balance. The Sun–Earth L1 point is about 1.5 million km sunward of Earth.
accepted.tq: Match the exact scientific term with its defining condition.
accepted.sec: Space science terms - Lagrange points, escape velocity, soft landing, Hohmann transfer

accepted.s: The Sun–Earth L1 point, used as the station for Aditya-L1, is located approximately:
o: 150 million km away from the Sun on the opposite side of Earth
5 million km south of the lunar orbit
accepted.x: The Sun–Earth L1 point is approximately 1.5 million km sunward of Earth and is the station associated with Aditya-L1.
accepted.tq: Use the directional qualifier and scale together to avoid confusing L1 with lunar or solar distances.
accepted.sec: Space science terms - Lagrange points, escape velocity, soft landing, Hohmann transfer

accepted.s: The minimum speed required for an object to escape the gravitational field of Earth is approximately:
accepted.x: Earth’s escape velocity is approximately 11.2 km/s.
accepted.tq: Check the decimal place carefully in a standard numerical value.
accepted.sec: Space science terms - Lagrange points, escape velocity, soft landing, Hohmann transfer

accepted.s: A Hohmann transfer is best described as:
o: A controlled low-speed touchdown on a planetary surface
A point of gravitational balance in a two-body system
A direct vertical launch requiring continuous engine thrust
A fuel-efficient transfer between two orbits using an elliptical orbit and two engine burns
accepted.x: A Hohmann transfer uses an elliptical transfer orbit and two engine burns to move between two orbits efficiently. Mangalyaan used this method to reach Mars.
accepted.tq: Match the operational description with the correct orbital-mechanics term.
accepted.sec: Space science terms - Lagrange points, escape velocity, soft landing, Hohmann transfer

accepted.s: Which of the following correctly describes the soft-landing limits of Chandrayaan-3?
o: Vertical speed not more than 2 km/s, horizontal speed not more than 0.5 km/s and slope not more than 12°
Vertical speed not more than 12 m/s, horizontal speed not more than 2 m/s and slope not more than 0.5°
Vertical speed not more than 2 m/s, horizontal speed not more than 0.5 m/s and slope not more than 12°
Vertical speed not more than 0.5 m/s, horizontal speed not more than 2 m/s and slope not more than 30°
accepted.x: The Chandrayaan-3 soft-landing limits were vertical speed up to 2 m/s, horizontal speed up to 0.5 m/s and slope up to 12 degrees.
accepted.tq: Keep the three limits aligned with their respective physical quantities and units.
accepted.sec: Space science terms - Lagrange points, escape velocity, soft landing, Hohmann transfer

accepted.s: Which one of the following statements about Chandrayaan-1 is correct?
o: It weighed 138 kg and carried five instruments from India alone.
It weighed 13,800 kg and carried only Indian instruments.
It weighed 1,380 kg and carried 11 instruments from India and other countries.
It weighed 1,380 kg and carried no international instruments.
accepted.x: Chandrayaan-1 had a mass of 1,380 kg and carried 11 instruments contributed by India, the USA, the UK, Germany, Sweden and Bulgaria.
accepted.tq: Test the mass, instrument count and international participation together.
accepted.sec: Chandrayaan-1 - Moon Impact Probe, payloads → discovery  [other exams, GROUP-II]

accepted.s: The Moon Impact Probe of Chandrayaan-1 reached the lunar south polar region on:
accepted.x: Chandrayaan-1’s Moon Impact Probe hit the lunar south polar region on 14 November 2008.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the impact date from the later Chandrayaan-1 contact-loss date and Mars-orbit date.
accepted.sec: Chandrayaan-1 - Moon Impact Probe, payloads → discovery  [other exams, GROUP-II]

accepted.s: Which instrument supplied evidence of water or hydroxyl on the Moon in the Chandrayaan-1 mission?
accepted.x: NASA’s Moon Mineralogy Mapper, or M3, provided evidence of water or hydroxyl on the Moon. The other listed instruments were associated with Mangalyaan.
accepted.tq: Separate similarly named instruments by their target body and mission.
accepted.sec: Chandrayaan-1 - Moon Impact Probe, payloads → discovery  [other exams, GROUP-II]

accepted.s: Which one of the following is NOT a payload of Chandrayaan-1?
accepted.x: TMC, Mini-SAR and CIXS were among the Chandrayaan-1 payloads. Lyman Alpha Photometer was one of Mangalyaan’s five payloads.
accepted.tq: Identify the instrument that belongs to the neighbouring Mars mission.
accepted.sec: Chandrayaan-1 - Moon Impact Probe, payloads → discovery  [other exams, GROUP-II]

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements regarding Chandrayaan-1:
1. It completed more than 3,400 orbits.
2. Contact with it was lost on 29 August 2009.
3. It operated for 312 days.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: Chandrayaan-1 completed over 3,400 orbits, operated for 312 days and lost contact on 29 August 2009. All three statements are correct.
accepted.tq: Verify the count, duration and termination date as separate factual components.
accepted.sec: Chandrayaan-1 - Moon Impact Probe, payloads → discovery  [other exams, GROUP-II]

accepted.s: India became the fourth nation to place its flag on the Moon through an impact probe. Which sequence lists the nations preceding India in this achievement?
accepted.x: India was the fourth nation to place its flag on the Moon through an impact probe, after the USSR, the USA and Japan.
accepted.tq: Use the stated rank and identify the preceding countries without substituting later lunar powers.
accepted.sec: Chandrayaan-1 - Moon Impact Probe, payloads → discovery  [other exams, GROUP-II]

accepted.s: Which one of the following sets contains only Chandrayaan-1 payloads?
o: MENCA, TIS, Mars Colour Camera and LAP
Methane Sensor for Mars, CIXS, SIR-2 and RADOM
accepted.x: TMC, HySI, LLRI and HEX were Chandrayaan-1 payloads. MENCA, TIS, Mars Colour Camera, LAP and the Methane Sensor for Mars were associated with Mangalyaan, while M3 and other instruments were mixed in the remaining options.
accepted.tq: Check every item in the set, not merely the first familiar instrument.
accepted.sec: Chandrayaan-1 - Moon Impact Probe, payloads → discovery  [other exams, GROUP-II]
